sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Durham, NC?
sections.html:
Durham County Tax Administration lists, assesses and collects property tax for homes inside the City of Durham, and the city sets only its own rate. The tax office is at 201 East Main Street, 3rd Floor, Administration Building II, Durham, NC 27701, open 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays, and its main number is 919-560-0300.

The city and county tax work together in collections. The county's foreclosure page says the Tax Collector acts at the direction of the county commissioners and the Durham City Council, and the lawsuits it files name the City and County of Durham as plaintiffs. Mailed payments go to Durham County Tax Collector, PO Box 3397, Durham, NC 27702-3397, and the county asks that no cash be mailed.

sections.h2: What are the Durham property tax rates?
sections.html:
For fiscal year 2026-27 the county prints a City of Durham rate of $0.4371 and a county rate of $0.5792, which combine to $1.0163. The city's own budget announcement says its rate stays at 43.71 cents per $100 of assessed value.

The county's reappraisal took effect January 1, 2025, and the 2025-2026 row is the first year printed after it. Look up the parcel on the county's tax site for the exact bill rather than relying on a combined figure.

sections.h2: When is Durham property tax due and when does interest start?
sections.html:
Durham real and personal property tax is due September 1, and the county says you can pay through January 5 without interest. January 6 starts delinquency, with 2% interest in the first month and three quarters of one percent for each month after, which tracks G.S. 105-360. When January 5 lands on a weekend, the next business day is the last day to pay.

  • Registered motor vehicles follow a different schedule, with 5% interest in the first month.
  • Monthly payment plans exist for real property bills only, and they must be arranged before the bill turns delinquent.
  • Payment plans do not remove a delinquent owner from the newspaper advertisement of unpaid taxes.
  • Card payments carry a processing fee, and electronic checks online are free.
  • If a mortgage company escrows your tax, it typically sends payment in late November.

sections.h2: How do I appeal my Durham property assessment?
sections.html:
You file with Durham County before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns from taking appeals. For the 2026 cycle that was June 17, 2026 at 5:00 p.m., so the window has closed for this year. The county recommends the online appeal on its Tax Help page, which also shows your appeal's status, and a paper Real Property Appeal form is available.

Durham County reappraised all real property effective January 1, 2025. The county tells owners that the only issue the tax office can address is the appraised value, not affordability, service levels or the change from the last reappraisal. In years between reappraisals the county may not change a parcel's value except for events such as a zoning change or a change in the physical features.

After the county board rules, a further appeal goes to the North Carolina Property Tax Commission, and the notice is filed within 30 days after the board mailed its decision, under G.S. 105-290. Personal property and motor vehicle appeals generally need to be filed within 30 days of the bill date.

sections.h2: What property tax relief can a Durham homeowner claim?
sections.html:
Durham County lists three homestead programs and applications are due June 1. Each owner may use only one of the three.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes the greater of $25,000 or 50% of the assessed value of the permanent residence, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled on January 1 of the tax year, with prior-year income not above $38,800. The county says a single application enrolls you.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: limits tax to 4% of income when income is within the limit, and 5% when it is above the limit but within 150% of it. The owner must have owned and lived in the home for five years, and a new application is needed every year.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: excludes up to the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit, and part of the form must be completed through the Department of Veterans Affairs.

The county also points to a separate Low Income Homeowner Relief program run through the Department of Social Services. Call 919-560-0300 for help with the forms. Deferred circuit breaker taxes come due on a disqualifying event such as a transfer, and the most recent three years are what must be paid, so a sale of the home triggers repayment.

sections.h2: What happens if Durham property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid real property tax becomes a lien and the county can foreclose through private attorneys under G.S. 105-374. The tax office tries notices and sometimes a payment plan first, then sends a pre-foreclosure letter before assigning the parcel to an attorney.

Once a parcel is assigned, the tax office stops taking direct payments and plans. Payment must go through the attorney and cover taxes, interest, fees and costs. Foreclosure sales run on the second Tuesday of each month at 12:00pm in the lobby of the Durham County Judicial Building, 510 Dillard Street.

  • The winning bidder posts a 10% deposit, and the sale stays open for 10 days for upset bids.
  • An owner, mortgage holder or other defendant can redeem by paying taxes, interest, fees and costs until the court confirms the sale and the deed is delivered.
  • The county says there is no real defense to a tax foreclosure complaint, since a superior lien cuts off junior liens and ownership rights.
  • Durham County does not sell tax liens, because the legislature ended that option in 1983.

sections.h2: How does Durham property tax affect selling my house?
sections.html:
The county bills the person who owned the parcel on January 1 for the whole year, and it advises a former owner to forward that bill to the new owner. In a mid-year sale, ask your closing attorney how the year's bill is prorated between seller and buyer.

Ask the Tax Collector for the balance before you set a closing date. If a lien from a delinquent year exists, the closing attorney needs the payoff in writing. Once a parcel has been assigned to a foreclosure attorney, the payoff comes only through that attorney, so request the figure early and build the closing date around it.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Durham?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table for Durham city lists these figures, which frame the value that the tax rates apply to.

  • Population: 305,561 in the July 2025 estimate, up 7.6% from the April 2020 base, across 112.79 square miles of land.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate of 52.3% and median owner-occupied value of $392,800 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Median household income of $81,619 and median gross rent of $1,508.
  • Households: 126,550, with 2.21 persons per household.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Durham property tax without interest?
faqs.a: January 5. Durham County bills are due September 1, and taxes paid after January 5 are delinquent. If January 5 falls on a weekend, the next business day is the last day. Registered motor vehicles do not follow this schedule.

faqs.q: Who sets the City of Durham property tax rate?
faqs.a: The Durham City Council sets the city rate through the annual budget. The county's Tax Rates page says each municipality's board determines its rate during budget adoption, concluding in mid to late June, with new rates effective July 1.

faqs.q: Can I set up a payment plan for Durham property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, for real property bills only, and only before the bill becomes delinquent. The county also notes that you can pay without a formal agreement until January 5.

faqs.q: Do I owe Durham tax on a house I sold after January 1?
faqs.a: Possibly. The county bills the owner of record as of January 1, even if that person sold afterward, and it advises forwarding the bill to the new owner. Ask the Tax Collector and your closing attorney how the bill is settled.

faqs.q: How do I stop a Durham tax foreclosure?
faqs.a: Redeem the parcel by paying taxes, interest, fees and costs to the attorney the county assigned. Redemption is allowed until the court confirms the sale and the deed is delivered, and a federal bankruptcy filing can also pause the process.
